children: U.S. regulators are lining up interviews with employees of Guggenheim Partners as they investigate potential wrongdoing at CEO Mark Walter's sprawling businesses, according to a media report on Thursday.

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has recently requested interviews with current and former employees of Guggenheim Investments, the $367B asset-managing arm of Guggenheim Partners, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Some of the people under focus have managed portfolios of assets for insurance companies, the report said.
Guggenheim Investments told Bloomberg that it's cooperating with the investigation.

The interviews demonstrate that regulators are continuing their probe even after assurances from officials at Guggenheim and TWG Global, Walter's holding company, that they're working to resolve government inquiries.
Last month, TWG defended itself from critics, saying there was no wrongdoing and "there is no victim here."

The investigation of Walter's empire expanded from a probe of accounting practices regarding the disclosure of revenue fees at Guggenheim's private funds unit last year. Then prosecutors started examining dealings at Walter's insurance companies, Bloomberg reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter. This year, two of the insurers said that more than $20B of loans should have been classified as affiliated transactions but weren't, Bloomberg said.
